events.description: The corporation issues common stock and receives cash from its new shareholders.

events.title: The company borrows from a bank

events.title: The company purchases equipment

events.title: The company serves customers
events.description: Customers pay cash for the services provided during the year.

events.title: The company pays employees

Income Statement.question: Which conclusion is supported by this income statement?
options: The company’s cash increased by \$18,000 because net income and cash change are the same.
The company earned net income of \$18,000 from its operations during the year.
The company ended the year with total assets of \$18,000.
Income Statement.correct: The company earned net income of \$18,000 from its operations during the year.
Income Statement.feedback: The statement supports a conclusion about operating performance. It does not, by itself, explain the change in cash or total assets.

Retained Earnings.question: Which statement best defines retained earnings?
options: Cash that management has formally reserved for future business use.
The cumulative net income earned since inception that has not been distributed to shareholders as dividends.
Amounts received from shareholders in exchange for common stock.
Retained Earnings.correct: The cumulative net income earned since inception that has not been distributed to shareholders as dividends.

Balance Sheet.question: Which statement best explains how the company financed its \$138,000 of assets?

Creditors have claims of \$20,000, and shareholders have claims of \$118,000.
Revenue of \$58,000 and expenses of \$40,000 account for all claims on the assets.
Balance Sheet.correct: Creditors have claims of \$20,000, and shareholders have claims of \$118,000.
Balance Sheet.feedback: Assets are the resources. Liabilities and stockholders’ equity identify the creditor and owner claims that financed those resources.

events.description: The corporation pays cash for rent, utilities, marketing, and other routine costs.
events.explanation: Routine costs incurred to generate revenue are operating activities and expenses.

events.title: The company pays a dividend
events.description: The board returns some cash to shareholders after the first year of business.
events.explanation: A dividend is a return to owners, so it is a financing activity. It is not an expense.

Income Statement.question: Which conclusion is supported by this income statement?
options: The company’s cash increased by \$29,000 because net income and cash change are the same.
The company earned net income of \$29,000 from its operations during the year.
The company ended the year with total assets of \$29,000.
Income Statement.correct: The company earned net income of \$29,000 from its operations during the year.
Income Statement.feedback: The statement supports a conclusion about operating performance. It does not, by itself, explain the change in cash or total assets.

Retained Earnings.question: Which statement best defines retained earnings?
options: Cash that management has formally reserved for future business use.
The cumulative net income earned since inception that has not been distributed to shareholders as dividends.
Amounts received from shareholders in exchange for common stock.
Retained Earnings.correct: The cumulative net income earned since inception that has not been distributed to shareholders as dividends.
Retained Earnings.feedback: Retained earnings represents cumulative earnings kept in the business. It is not a cash reserve, and shareholder contributions are reported separately as common stock.

Balance Sheet.question: Which statement best explains how the company financed its \$139,000 of assets?
options: Cash and equipment identify the outside sources that financed all of the company’s assets.
Creditors have claims of \$80,000, and shareholders have claims of \$59,000.
Revenue of \$100,000 and expenses of \$71,000 account for all claims on the assets.
Balance Sheet.correct: Creditors have claims of \$80,000, and shareholders have claims of \$59,000.
Balance Sheet.feedback: Assets are the resources. Liabilities and stockholders’ equity identify the creditor and owner claims that financed those resources.

Statement of Cash Flows.question: What does the statement of cash flows add to the financial picture?
options: It measures operating success by comparing revenues with expenses.
It reports the company’s resources and the creditor and owner claims on those resources at a point in time.
It explains how operating, investing, and financing activities changed cash during the period.
Statement of Cash Flows.correct: It explains how operating, investing, and financing activities changed cash during the period.
Statement of Cash Flows.feedback: The statement of cash flows explains the change in cash by business activity. Profitability and financial position are communicated by other statements.
